title: Luke Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 16.

questions.question: In Luke 16, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The steward is accused of wasting goods
The steward calls the lord's debtors
The lord commends the unjust steward
Jesus says to make friends with the mammon of unrighteousness
questions.correctAnswer: The steward is accused of wasting goods
questions.explanation: The steward being accused is the first event mentioned in Luke 16:1.

questions.question: Who was accused of wasting his goods in Luke 16?
questions.explanation: The steward was accused of wasting his goods according to Luke 16:1.

questions.question: What did the lord tell the steward to do after hearing the accusation?
options: Give an account of thy stewardship
questions.correctAnswer: Give an account of thy stewardship
questions.explanation: The lord told the steward to give an account of his stewardship in Luke 16:2.

questions.question: Why was the steward worried in Luke 16?
options: Because his lord was taking away his stewardship
Because he was accused of stealing
questions.correctAnswer: Because his lord was taking away his stewardship
questions.explanation: The steward was worried because his lord was taking away his stewardship as stated in Luke 16:3.

questions.question: What two things did the steward say he could not do?
questions.explanation: The steward said he could not dig and was ashamed to beg in Luke 16:3.

questions.question: What did the steward plan to do after losing his stewardship?
options: Make friends so they might receive him into their houses
questions.correctAnswer: Make friends so they might receive him into their houses
questions.explanation: The steward resolved to make friends to be received into their houses in Luke 16:4.

questions.question: To whom did the steward call to settle debts?
questions.explanation: The steward called every one of his lord's debtors as per Luke 16:5.

questions.question: How much oil did the first debtor owe the lord?
questions.explanation: The first debtor owed an hundred measures of oil according to Luke 16:6.

questions.question: What amount did the steward instruct the first debtor to write on his bill?
questions.explanation: The steward told the first debtor to write fifty on his bill in Luke 16:6.

questions.question: How much wheat did the second debtor owe the lord?
questions.explanation: The second debtor owed an hundred measures of wheat as found in Luke 16:7.

questions.question: What amount did the steward tell the second debtor to write on his bill?
questions.explanation: The steward instructed the second debtor to write fourscore on his bill in Luke 16:7.

questions.question: The lord commended the steward because he had done what?
questions.explanation: The lord commended the unjust steward because he had done wisely according to Luke 16:8.

questions.question: Jesus said to make friends with the mammon of unrighteousness so that when you fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.
questions.explanation: This statement is directly from Luke 16:9.

questions.question: The steward was praised for being honest in handling true riches.
questions.explanation: The steward was commended for doing wisely with unrighteous mammon, not for honesty with true riches (Luke 16:8-11).

questions.question: The text says the steward was afraid to call the lord's debtors because they might refuse him.
questions.explanation: The text does not say the steward was afraid to call the debtors; rather he called them and reduced their debts (Luke 16:5-7).

medium.title: Luke Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Luke 16:13, what is impossible for a servant to do?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:13 states that no servant can serve two masters, as he will hate one and love the other or hold to one and despise the other.

questions.question: What does Luke 16:11 promise will happen if someone is faithful in the unrighteous mammon as commanded in Luke 16:10?
options: They will be entrusted with true riches
They will be given earthly treasures
questions.correctAnswer: They will be entrusted with true riches
questions.explanation: Luke 16:11 explains that if you are faithful in the unrighteous mammon (as Luke 16:10 commands being faithful in little), you will be entrusted with true riches.

questions.question: According to Luke 16:15, what does God know that men justify themselves before others by?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:15 says God knows the hearts of men, even though men justify themselves before others, indicating the true condition is known only by God.

questions.question: How does Luke 16:16 relate to Luke 16:17 in explaining the permanence of the law?
options: The kingdom is preached since John, but the law still stands
The law ended with John and is no longer binding
The law is easier to break than heaven and earth to pass
The prophets replaced the law after John
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom is preached since John, but the law still stands
questions.explanation: Luke 16:16 states the law and prophets were until John, since then the kingdom is preached, and Luke 16:17 emphasizes that it is easier for heaven and earth to pass than one jot of the law to fail, affirming its permanence.

questions.question: What lesson about faithfulness does Luke 16:12 teach about handling another man's possessions?
options: If not faithful with another's possessions, you will not receive your own
You should take what you can from another's possessions
Being faithful with your own possessions is enough
Faithfulness is only required in spiritual matters
questions.correctAnswer: If not faithful with another's possessions, you will not receive your own
questions.explanation: Luke 16:12 states that if you are not faithful in what belongs to another, no one will entrust you with what is your own, emphasizing responsibility and trustworthiness.

questions.question: According to Luke 16:14, what was the reaction of the covetous Pharisees to Jesus' teaching?
options: They reported him to the authorities
questions.explanation: Luke 16:14 describes that the covetous Pharisees heard Jesus' words and derided him, showing their rejection of his teaching.

questions.question: What does Luke 16:18 say about the one who marries a divorced woman?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:18 clearly states that whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery, highlighting the seriousness of marriage covenant.

questions.question: What condition did Lazarus suffer from as described in Luke 16:20-21?
options: He was full of sores and desired crumbs from the rich man's table
He was blind and begging for alms
He was paralyzed and unable to move
questions.correctAnswer: He was full of sores and desired crumbs from the rich man's table
questions.explanation: Luke 16:20-21 describes Lazarus as a beggar full of sores who longed to be fed with the crumbs falling from the rich man's table.

questions.question: What does Luke 16:9 instruct believers to do with the mammon of unrighteousness?
options: Make friends with it to receive you into everlasting habitations
Use it to gain earthly power
questions.correctAnswer: Make friends with it to receive you into everlasting habitations
questions.explanation: Luke 16:9 advises making friends with unrighteous mammon so that when it fails, they may receive you into eternal dwellings, emphasizing wise stewardship.

questions.question: What does Luke 16:15 say about what is highly esteemed among men in God's sight?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:15 clearly states that what is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God, revealing the contrast between human and divine values.

questions.question: How does Luke 16:10 connect faithfulness in little things to greater responsibilities?
options: Faithful in little is faithful in much; unjust in little is unjust in much
Greater responsibilities are given regardless of faithfulness
Unjust in little can be just in much
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful in little is faithful in much; unjust in little is unjust in much
questions.explanation: Luke 16:10 teaches that faithfulness or unfaithfulness in small matters reflects on greater matters, encouraging integrity at all levels.

questions.question: What does Luke 16:22 say happened to the beggar Lazarus after death?
options: He was carried by angels into Abraham's bosom
He was buried with the rich man
questions.correctAnswer: He was carried by angels into Abraham's bosom
questions.explanation: Luke 16:22 states that after death, Lazarus was carried by angels into Abraham's bosom, indicating a place of comfort and honor.

questions.question: According to Luke 16:17, which is easier: for heaven and earth to pass or for one tittle of the law to fail?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:17 asserts it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one jot of the law to fail, emphasizing the enduring nature of God's law.

questions.question: The steward in Luke 16:1-2 was praised by his lord for wasting his goods.
questions.explanation: Luke 16:1-2 shows the steward was accused of wasting his lord's goods and was called to give an account, so he was not praised for wasting them.

questions.question: According to Luke 16:13, it is possible for a servant to serve God and mammon simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Luke 16:13 clearly states that no servant can serve two masters, specifically that one cannot serve God and mammon simultaneously.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 16.

questions.question: In Luke 16:23, where is the rich man described as lifting up his eyes?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:23 states, 'And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments...,' showing the rich man is in hell.

questions.question: According to Luke 16:24, what did the rich man ask Father Abraham to do?
options: Send Lazarus to warn his brothers
Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water to cool his tongue
Give him a second chance on earth
questions.correctAnswer: Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water to cool his tongue
questions.explanation: Luke 16:24 records the rich man requesting, 'send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.'

questions.question: What reason does Abraham give in Luke 16:25 for the rich man's torment?
options: He did not believe in God
He received good things in his lifetime, while Lazarus received evil things
He refused to help Lazarus when alive
questions.correctAnswer: He received good things in his lifetime, while Lazarus received evil things
questions.explanation: In Luke 16:25, Abraham says, 'Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.'

questions.question: What does Luke 16:26 say is fixed between the place of torment and comfort?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:26 states, 'And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed,' making clear the impassable separation.

questions.question: In Luke 16:29, what does Abraham say the rich man's brethren already have?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:29 records Abraham saying, 'They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them,' referring to the Old Testament scriptures.

questions.question: According to Luke 16:31, what will happen if people do not listen to Moses and the prophets?
options: They will be persuaded by a sign from heaven
They will be persuaded if one rises from the dead
They will not be persuaded even if one rises from the dead
questions.correctAnswer: They will not be persuaded even if one rises from the dead
questions.explanation: Luke 16:31 says, 'If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead,' emphasizing the sufficiency of scripture.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'torments' (Luke 16:23) mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek term used in Luke 16:23 for 'torments' is 'basanisthentes,' which means severe suffering or torment, not just physical pain or temporary discomfort.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31)?
questions.explanation: The parable functions as typology, illustrating spiritual truths about afterlife and justice through symbolic characters (Luke 16:19-31).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage relates to the theme of Moses and the prophets mentioned in Luke 16:29?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:15 speaks of a prophet like Moses whom people should heed, connecting to the reference to Moses and the prophets in Luke 16:29.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of resurrection mentioned in Luke 16:31?
questions.explanation: John 11:25 has Jesus declaring himself the resurrection and the life, echoing the theme of resurrection's role in repentance from Luke 16:31.

questions.question: What event precedes the rich man seeing Abraham and Lazarus in Luke 16:23?
questions.explanation: Luke 16:22 says, 'the rich man also died, and was buried;' immediately preceding Luke 16:23 where he sees Abraham and Lazarus.

questions.question: In Luke 16:24, what cultural practice is illustrated by the rich man's request for water to cool his tongue?
options: A common method of relief from thirst in Jewish culture
questions.correctAnswer: A common method of relief from thirst in Jewish culture
questions.explanation: Requesting water to cool one's tongue was a recognized practice for relief from thirst and suffering, reflected in Luke 16:24 showing the rich man's torment.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'great gulf fixed' described in Luke 16:26 in Jewish eschatology?
options: It signifies the final separation between the righteous and the wicked after death
It represents a physical river in Sheol
It is a metaphor for the Jordan River
It indicates the separation between angels and humans
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the final separation between the righteous and the wicked after death
questions.explanation: In Jewish eschatology, the 'great gulf fixed' in Luke 16:26 symbolizes the irreversible divide between salvation and condemnation after death.

questions.question: How does the parable of the rich man and Lazarus function as an inclusio in Luke 16?
options: It begins and ends with references to Moses and the prophets
It starts and finishes with the theme of wealth and stewardship
It frames the chapter with themes of justice and eternal destiny
It opens and closes with the character of Lazarus
questions.correctAnswer: It frames the chapter with themes of justice and eternal destiny
questions.explanation: The parable serves as an inclusio by enclosing the chapter with themes of justice, stewardship, and eternal consequence (Luke 16:1-31).

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 16:27-28, the rich man asks Abraham to send Lazarus to warn his five brothers to avoid torment.
questions.explanation: Luke 16:27-28 shows the rich man asking Abraham to send Lazarus to his father's house to testify to his five brothers to prevent their torment.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 16:13 teach about the nature of human allegiance in relation to God and worldly wealth?
options: No servant can serve two masters; one will inevitably love one and hate the other
It is possible to serve God and mammon equally without conflict
Serving mammon is a necessary step to eventually serve God
Allegiance to God is secondary to managing worldly wealth wisely
questions.correctAnswer: No servant can serve two masters; one will inevitably love one and hate the other
questions.explanation: Luke 16:13 states that no servant can serve two masters, emphasizing the impossibility of divided loyalty between God and mammon, teaching exclusive allegiance to God.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine judgment and human self-justification is taught in Luke 16:15?
options: God knows the hearts and condemns self-justification before men as abomination
Human self-justification is acceptable if it is esteemed by men
God judges only external actions, not the heart
Justification before men guarantees justification before God
questions.correctAnswer: God knows the hearts and condemns self-justification before men as abomination
questions.explanation: Luke 16:15 teaches that God knows the hearts and considers those who justify themselves before men as detestable, emphasizing divine omniscience and judgment beyond human appearances.

questions.question: What doctrine about the continuity and fulfillment of Scripture is conveyed in Luke 16:16?
options: The law and the prophets were until John; since then the kingdom of God is preached
The law and prophets continue unchanged and exclusive of the kingdom message
John’s ministry replaced the law and prophets entirely
The kingdom of God is unrelated to the law and prophets
questions.correctAnswer: The law and the prophets were until John; since then the kingdom of God is preached
questions.explanation: Luke 16:16 affirms that the era of the law and prophets culminated with John the Baptist, and from then the kingdom of God is preached, indicating fulfillment and transition in redemptive history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 16:15 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The verse states God knows the hearts, illustrating His attribute of omniscience—complete and perfect knowledge of human inner motives.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 16:24 specifically demonstrate in the context of the rich man's plea?
questions.explanation: The verse shows the rich man in torment, illustrating God’s justice in punishing unrepentant sin.

questions.question: How does the parable in Luke 16:19-31 connect thematically to the teaching of Jesus on the final judgment elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It emphasizes eternal conscious punishment and reversal of earthly fortunes
It denies the existence of an afterlife
It teaches universal salvation regardless of earthly conduct
It focuses solely on temporal justice without eternal consequences
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes eternal conscious punishment and reversal of earthly fortunes
questions.explanation: The parable illustrates the reversal of fortunes after death and eternal consequences, consistent with final judgment teachings in Matthew 25.

questions.question: In what way does Luke 16:8 prepare for the New Testament teaching on wisdom and prudence in the stewardship of worldly resources?
options: It commends shrewdness in using worldly resources for eternal purposes
It encourages dishonesty to gain riches
It discourages prudent management of possessions
It promotes wealth accumulation as a sign of divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: It commends shrewdness in using worldly resources for eternal purposes
questions.explanation: The verse commends the steward’s shrewdness, teaching believers to wisely use earthly resources to gain eternal friends, foreshadowing stewardship theology.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 16:10 and Luke 16:11 teach about faithfulness and stewardship?
options: Faithfulness in small matters demonstrates readiness for greater spiritual responsibility
Unfaithfulness in small matters is irrelevant to spiritual trust
Faithfulness is only required in spiritual, not material matters
Stewardship is unrelated to spiritual faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness in small matters demonstrates readiness for greater spiritual responsibility
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that faithfulness in minor or worldly things is a prerequisite for receiving true spiritual riches and responsibilities.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 16:24 and Luke 16:26 teach about the nature of the afterlife and intercession after death?
options: There is a fixed gulf between the saved and the lost, preventing intercession after death
The dead can be sent back to warn the living
The afterlife is temporary and reversible by prayer
Intercession from the dead is the means of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: There is a fixed gulf between the saved and the lost, preventing intercession after death
questions.explanation: These verses describe a great fixed gulf that cannot be crossed, denying the possibility of post-mortem intercession or crossing between realms.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 16:29 and Luke 16:31 teach about the sufficiency of Scripture and the response to miraculous signs?
options: Hearing Moses and the prophets is sufficient for repentance; even a resurrection will not persuade if Scripture is rejected
Miraculous signs are required for genuine faith
Scripture is insufficient without signs and wonders
Repentance is only possible through a resurrected messenger
questions.correctAnswer: Hearing Moses and the prophets is sufficient for repentance; even a resurrection will not persuade if Scripture is rejected
questions.explanation: Abraham’s reply affirms that the Scriptures (Moses and prophets) are sufficient for repentance, and rejecting them means even a resurrection won’t convince.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Luke 16:22-31 teaches universal salvation because the rich man and Lazarus both die and have interaction. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches eternal conscious punishment for the unrighteous and eternal comfort for the righteous
It teaches that after death all souls eventually reunite in peace
It teaches purgatorial purification for the rich man
It denies any conscious existence after death
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches eternal conscious punishment for the unrighteous and eternal comfort for the righteous
questions.explanation: The passage clearly depicts torment for the rich man and comfort for Lazarus, indicating conscious existence and eternal destinies after death.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 16:12 teach about stewardship and ownership in the context of Christian discipleship?
options: Faithfulness in another's possessions is prerequisite to receiving one’s own
Faithfulness in spiritual matters does not require material stewardship
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness in another's possessions is prerequisite to receiving one’s own
questions.explanation: The verse teaches that if one is not faithful in what belongs to another, one will not be entrusted with true ownership, emphasizing stewardship responsibility.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted by God's refusal to allow crossing the 'great gulf' in Luke 16:26?
questions.explanation: The fixed gulf symbolizes God's justice in maintaining the separation between the saved and the lost, enforcing eternal consequences.

questions.question: Which theological theme does Luke 16:9 teach about the use of material wealth in relation to eternal salvation?
options: Use unrighteous mammon to make friends who will receive you into everlasting habitations
Material possessions should be ignored in spiritual life
Accumulation of wealth is the ultimate goal of the Christian
questions.correctAnswer: Use unrighteous mammon to make friends who will receive you into everlasting habitations
questions.explanation: The verse teaches the wise use of worldly wealth to secure eternal relationships, highlighting stewardship for eternal benefit.

questions.question: How does Luke 16:17 contribute to the doctrine of the permanence of God's law in contrast to changing human customs?
options: It affirms that not even the smallest part of the law will fail, emphasizing its permanence
It suggests the law can be changed to fit new eras
It implies heaven and earth will pass before the law is fulfilled by human effort
It indicates the law is obsolete after Christ
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that not even the smallest part of the law will fail, emphasizing its permanence
questions.explanation: The verse states it is easier for heaven and earth to pass than for a tittle of the law to fail, teaching the law’s enduring validity.
